raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The ROCm `AWQLinearKernel.apply` path expands the entire weight matrix with `awq_dequantize_triton`, then calls `torch.matmul` on every invocation. `awq_gemm_triton` already exists, but no runtime caller uses it.

This is expensive during decode. I encountered it while tracing the [official Ternary Bonsai AWQ checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-AWQ-4bit/tree/7f49f5d23a09087131cd50627366967f013b9f9e). Its sampled attention and MLP weights use only codes 7, 8 and 9 with zero point 8, but the generic AWQ path still materializes a full floating-point matrix.

## Modifications

- Route gfx1151 ROCm AWQ batches of 1 through 16 rows to the existing packed Triton GEMM with a 16x64x32 tile and split-K 8. Larger batches, other HIP architectures, and CUDA/Marlin routing stay unchanged. CDNA does not take the new path without CDNA measurements.
- Accumulate in FP32 and retain FP32 split-K partials. The existing helper used the output dtype for both, which could overflow on FP16 inputs even when the final answer was finite.
- Reduce split-K partials directly into the activation dtype. Avoid the initial zero-fill and skip reduction for split-K 1.
- Allow BF16 activations on the ROCm AWQ path. Keep checkpoint weights, zero points and scales unchanged. No activation quantization or ternary-specific repacking is introduced.
- Add kernel tests, runtime dispatch coverage for strided/empty/batched inputs and bias, and a paired benchmark. Defer unrelated Quark AITER imports until the operations that need them, so AWQ runtime imports do not require AITER.

## Accuracy tests

On Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.53211, Torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2 and Triton 3.8.0:

```sh
python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_awq_gemm.py -q
# 18 passed in 4.34s
```

Coverage includes FP16/BF16, group sizes 32/64/128/full-K, split-K 1/8, tail output columns, signed packed words, exact agreement between dequantization implementations, and a cancellation case that needs FP32 accumulation.

On the real Bonsai tensor panels below, relative squared error against FP32 matmul of the same dequantized operands was 2.64e-6 for the BF16 attention tensor, 2.75e-6 for the BF16 gate tensor, and 4.27e-8 for the FP16 gate tensor. The dequantize-plus-matmul reference has essentially the same output-rounding error. Reduction order changes, so outputs are not promised bit-identical.

The registered HIP `test_linear_dispatch` now passes on gfx1151, including packed rows 1/16, fallback rows 0/17, BF16/FP16, strided input and bias. A gfx942 architecture control checks that CDNA does not select packed GEMM. Sixteen more cases load both pinned Bonsai layer-0 matrix tensors and compare runtime outputs with FP32 decoded-weight matmul; relative squared errors are below 1e-4 with generated activations. These are layer-level checks, not a full Bonsai model forward. Quark AITER imports have been moved to their operation boundaries, without installing or stubbing AITER. This PR remains a draft pending complete-model or server accuracy acceptance. CDNA performance is unmeasured and CDNA retains the existing fallback, so no CDNA speedup is claimed.

## Speed tests and profiling

Paired GPU-graph timing, nine rounds with alternating arm order and 40 calls per graph, on the hardware above. Actual checkpoint weight tensors are pinned to revision `7f49f5d23a09087131cd50627366967f013b9f9e`; activation inputs are generated with seed 917, not captured model activations. Times include dequantization and matmul in the reference, and packed GEMM plus split reduction in the candidate.

| Weight tensor | M | dtype | K x N | Dequantize + matmul | Packed GEMM | Median paired ratio |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Layer 0 linear attention `in_proj_qkv` | 1 | BF16 | 5120 x 10240 | 1222.43 us | 169.60 us | 7.22x |
| Layer 0 MLP `gate_proj` | 16 | BF16 | 5120 x 17408 | 2116.53 us | 321.31 us | 6.65x |
| Layer 0 MLP `gate_proj` | 1 | FP16 | 5120 x 17408 | 2089.41 us | 279.21 us | 7.48x |

A synthetic 512x1024 ternary AWQ matrix at M=1 took 18.56 vs 6.42 us, 2.89x paired. General random 4-bit weights at 5120x5120 took 564.05 vs 87.43 us at M=1, and 559.33 vs 93.99 us at M=16.

Clock and package-power telemetry was retained with the local panels. The machine had other CPU work, roughly 2 to 3 busy host cores during the real-tensor panels, so these are paired measurements under shared-package load rather than quiet or fixed-clock results. These are linear-operation timings, not end-to-end serving throughput or a comparison with CUDA Marlin.

The included benchmark reproduces the comparison using generated AWQ weights, including the same ternary codes:

```sh
python test/manual/bench_awq_gemm.py --m 1 --k 5120 --n 10240 --dtype bfloat16 --ternary
python test/manual/bench_awq_gemm.py --m 16 --k 5120 --n 17408 --dtype bfloat16 --ternary
```


The checkpoint qweight payload SHA-256 identities are `7e9f99e86381af9d9464a5f0c6332261473146aeb1ee563e376f9771953aeef5` for attention and `af7acf07e460940777e7c993e5d075c616a910f6fc2cc65dbb42679f21451cb6` for gate. The measured kernel source SHA-256 is `fdc3173733796b53c940ec29f9b1279704b56075e65384b6d5de269bc475c55b`.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Changed files pass the repository's isort/ruff formatting and lint settings, plus `git diff --check`.
- [x] Added focused kernel tests and runtime dispatch coverage. The 18 kernel checks and registered HIP dispatch test passed locally, as did 16 real-weight layer cases.
- [x] Added a standalone paired benchmark and reported exact scope and numerical errors.
- [ ] Complete-model or server accuracy acceptance before leaving draft. CDNA performance remains a separate requirement before enabling CDNA packed dispatch.

nodes.body:
This PR touches three things that other open PRs also change. Pointing them out in case it helps to split it so the AWQ part can land on its own:

1. **`setup_rocm.py` (gfx1151 in the allowlist, `AMDGPU_TARGET` precedence).**
   - Adding a wave32 target to the allowlist alone is not enough. Host launch code still sizes the sgl-kernel MoE top-k launches for a 64-lane wave. On gfx1201, an allowlist-only build of `main` aborts in `test_moe_topk_softmax` and hits `hipErrorLaunchFailure` in `test_moe_topk_sigmoid` (table in my comment on #43679), and gfx1151 is wave32 as well.
   - #43679 makes those launches use the device's wave size and covers gfx1100/1101/1102/1200/1201. I measured it: all 7 kernel test groups pass on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Adding `gfx1151` to its `supported_targets` would be the natural place for this.
   - #46901 makes an explicit `AMDGPU_TARGET` take precedence over autodetection, which is the same change as here.
2. **Quark schemes importing aiter lazily.** This is the same change as #46914 on `amd_march`, where RDNA work currently lands. On `main` I don't have a competing PR, so this part can stay here, but the two will need to agree.
3. **Packed AWQ GEMM for small batches.** This is the part unique to this PR. It is gated to gfx1151, so it is a no-op on the RDNA3/RDNA4 cards I can test. If you want a gfx1100/gfx1201 data point with the gate widened, I can run it.

+"""Compare packed AWQ GEMM with dequantize + matmul on the same inputs.
+
+Example:
+    python test/manual/bench_awq_gemm.py --k 5120 --n 17408 --m 16 --ternary
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.awq_triton import (
+    awq_dequantize_triton,
+    awq_gemm_triton,
+)
+
+
+def make_inputs(args):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
+    x = torch.randn((args.m, args.k), dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    shape = (args.k, args.n // 8)
+    if args.ternary:
+        qweight = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        for shift in range(0, 32, 4):
+            qweight |= (
+                torch.randint(7, 10, shape, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") << shift
+            )
+        qzeros = torch.full(
+            (args.k // args.group_size, args.n // 8),
+            -2004318072,  # 0x88888888 interpreted as int32
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+    else:
+        qweight = torch.randint(
+            -(2**31), 2**31 - 1, shape, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        )
+        qzeros = torch.randint(
+            -(2**31),
+            2**31 - 1,
+            (args.k // args.group_size, args.n // 8),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+    scales = (
+        torch.rand((args.k // args.group_size, args.n), dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+        * 0.05
+    )
+    return x, qweight, scales, qzeros
+
+
+def measure_paired(functions, rounds=9, repeats=40):
+    graphs = {}
+    for name, fn in functions.items():
+        for _ in range(3):
+            fn()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            for _ in range(repeats):
+                fn()
+        graphs[name] = graph
+    for _ in range(8):
+        for graph in graphs.values():
+            graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    samples = []
+    names = list(functions)
+    for i in range(rounds):
+        row = {}
+        for name in names[:: 1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1]:
+            start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            graphs[name].replay()
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            row[name] = start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / repeats
+        samples.append(row)
+    return samples
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--m", type=int, default=1)
+    parser.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=5120)
+    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10240)
+    parser.add_argument("--group-size", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float16", "bfloat16"], default="float16")
+    parser.add_argument("--ternary", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    x, qweight, scales, qzeros = make_inputs(args)
+    functions = {
+        "dequantize_matmul": lambda: x @ awq_dequantize_triton(qweight, scales, qzeros),
+        "packed_gemm": lambda: awq_gemm_triton(
+            x,
+            qweight,
+            scales,
+            qzeros,
+            split_k_iters=8,
+            block_size_m=16,
+            block_size_n=64,
+            block_size_k=32,
+        ),
+    }
+    reference = x.float() @ awq_dequantize_triton(qweight, scales, qzeros).float()
+    errors = {
+        name: (
+            (fn().float() - reference).square().sum() / reference.square().sum()
+        ).item()
+        for name, fn in functions.items()
+    }
+    samples = measure_paired(functions)
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+                "torch": torch.__version__,
+                "hip": torch.version.hip,
+                "config": vars(args),
+                "relative_squared_error": errors,
+                "samples_us": samples,
+                "median_us": {
+                    name: statistics.median(r[name] for r in samples)
+                    for name in functions
+                },
+                "paired_speedup": statistics.median(
+                    r["dequantize_matmul"] / r["packed_gemm"] for r in samples
+                ),
+            },
+            indent=2,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.awq_triton import (
+    awq_dequantize_decomposition,
+    awq_dequantize_triton,
+    awq_gemm_triton,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=5, suite="stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("group_size", [32, 64, 128, 512])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("split_k", [1, 8])
+def test_gemm_activation_dtypes(dtype, group_size, split_k):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    x = torch.randn((3, 512), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    qweight = torch.randint(
+        -(2**31), 2**31 - 1, (512, 9), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    qzeros = torch.randint(
+        -(2**31),
+        2**31 - 1,
+        (512 // group_size, 9),
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    scales = torch.rand((512 // group_size, 72), device="cuda", dtype=dtype) * 0.05
+    weight = awq_dequantize_decomposition(qweight, scales, qzeros)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        awq_dequantize_triton(qweight, scales, qzeros), weight, atol=0, rtol=0
+    )
+    expected = (x.float() @ weight.float()).to(dtype)
+    actual = awq_gemm_triton(
+        x,
+        qweight,
+        scales,
+        qzeros,
+        split_k,
+        block_size_m=16,
+        block_size_n=64,
+    )
+    assert actual.dtype == dtype
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0.015, rtol=0.01)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("split_k", [1, 8])
+def test_gemm_fp32_accumulation(split_k):
+    # Each half overflows FP16, although the complete dot product is zero.
+    x = torch.full((1, 4096), 512.0, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
+    x[:, 2048:] = -512.0
+    qweight = torch.full((4096, 8), 0x11111111, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    qzeros = torch.zeros((32, 8), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    scales = torch.ones((32, 64), dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
+    actual = awq_gemm_triton(
+        x,
+        qweight,
+        scales,
+        qzeros,
+        split_k,
+        block_size_m=16,
+        block_size_n=64,
+    )
+    assert torch.isfinite(actual).all()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, torch.zeros_like(actual), atol=0.002, rtol=0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

issue_comments.body:
This PR touches three things that other open PRs also change. Pointing them out in case it helps to split it so the AWQ part can land on its own:

1. **`setup_rocm.py` (gfx1151 in the allowlist, `AMDGPU_TARGET` precedence).**
   - Adding a wave32 target to the allowlist alone is not enough. Host launch code still sizes the sgl-kernel MoE top-k launches for a 64-lane wave. On gfx1201, an allowlist-only build of `main` aborts in `test_moe_topk_softmax` and hits `hipErrorLaunchFailure` in `test_moe_topk_sigmoid` (table in my comment on #43679), and gfx1151 is wave32 as well.
   - #43679 makes those launches use the device's wave size and covers gfx1100/1101/1102/1200/1201. I measured it: all 7 kernel test groups pass on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Adding `gfx1151` to its `supported_targets` would be the natural place for this.
   - #46901 makes an explicit `AMDGPU_TARGET` take precedence over autodetection, which is the same change as here.
2. **Quark schemes importing aiter lazily.** This is the same change as #46914 on `amd_march`, where RDNA work currently lands. On `main` I don't have a competing PR, so this part can stay here, but the two will need to agree.
3. **Packed AWQ GEMM for small batches.** This is the part unique to this PR. It is gated to gfx1151, so it is a no-op on the RDNA3/RDNA4 cards I can test. If you want a gfx1100/gfx1201 data point with the gate widened, I can run it.
